newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end with steep losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end with steep losses.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply lower and near the lowest levels of the session set in late trading.
December S&P 500s broke below support in the final 15 minutes, which traders saw as a negative for Friday's outlook.
The nearby S&P contract broke below support at 704.50, the trendline from the lows over the past six days, and below 704.10, which was the low on Wednesday.
"The only thing that would have been worse (for the outlook) would have been a very weak NASDAQ close," said Kevin O'Brien, stock index futures analyst at Prudential Securities.
O'Brien said he now has near-term target of 702.00 and 697.00 in the nearby S&P 500 contract.
Selling began in afternoon dealings when followthrough buying failed to develop as Treasury bond futures prices reached the highs of the day late in their session, traders said.

As prices slipped, the premium of December S&Ps over the spot index narrowed. Arbitrage sell programs were triggered when the premium of nearby S&Ps over the index dipped below 2.75 points, traders said.
Futures had traded lower in early dealings, but prices quickly rebounded when bond prices firmed in tandem with a rise in some technology stocks and slightly firmer bond prices.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures ended lower following declines in the cash index overnight and pressure on U.S. equities.

At settlement, December S&P 500s were off 7.30 points at 703.75, Russell 2000s eased 1.70 point to 343.50, Value Line futures were off 4.10 point to 645.60, Nikkei 225 index futures eased 155.0 to 20,910.0 and Midcap 400s eased 1.20 points to 244.15.
